title: Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI
intro: The everyday editing moves in the Tracks area: selecting, trimming, splitting, joining and moving regions.

tips.t: Trim to the playhead from either direction
tips.d: The commands are “Set Region/Event/Marquee Start to Playhead Position” and the matching End command — search the Key Commands window for “Playhead Position” and put them on keys. (Note that on audio regions the Start command also moves the region anchor to the playhead.) Related one-shot trims live under Edit > Trim, such as Region End to Next Region. No mouse precision needed.

src.label: Apple — Resize regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Snap Regions to Relative Value for off-grid parts
tips.d: By default, Logic's Snap menu is set to Snap Regions to Absolute Value: a moved item snaps exactly to the nearest grid position. For a region that sits deliberately off-grid, choose Snap > Snap Regions to Relative Value in the Tracks area menu bar. It keeps its distance from the grid: a region at 2.1.1.16 moved one beat forward lands on 2.2.1.16, not 2.2.1.1.

src.label: Apple — Snap items to the grid in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: T opens the Tool menu, T again closes it
tips.d: Press T to open the Tool menu at the pointer — Apple's default key command for Show Tool Menu. Press T again to close it.

src.label: Apple — Key commands for Tool Menu in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Logic has two Tool menus: Left-click and Command-click. Choose a tool from the Command-click Tool menu, then hold ⌘ to use it. Let go and you are back on your Left-click tool.

tips.t: Select everything after this point in one keystroke
tips.d: Press ⇧F (Select All Following) to select everything that comes after the current selection. That puts you one keystroke from moving the rest of the song.

tips.t: Lock events so tempo changes cannot move them
tips.d: Lock SMPTE Position keeps events at their absolute time when you change the tempo later. In the Event List, select events and choose Functions > Lock SMPTE Position, or Control-click and choose it from the shortcut menu; a padlock appears in the Lock column. Lock a region and every event inside it is locked. It requires Enable Complete Features in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced.
